artists.biography: The Mighty Mighty Bosstones were a ska punk band from Boston, Massachusetts, United States (Bosstones is a play on Boston). Their last lineup was Dicky Barrett (vocals), Joe Gittleman (bass), Lawrence Katz (guitar), Ben Carr (dancer, "Bosstone"), Joe Sirois (drums), Timothy "Johnny Vegas" Burton (saxophone), Kevin Leaner (saxophone) and Chris Rhodes (trombone) Formed in 1985, The Mighty Mighty Bosstones started playing in Boston clubs in the mid-1980s. After a brief period of inactivity due to the schooling commitments of its members, they reformed and released their album Devil's Night Out on Taang! Records. The Bosstones toured relentlessly throughout the 1990s, playing hundreds of shows a year, releasing albums and spinning off the popular rock radio hit "Someday I Suppose". They were eventually signed to Mercury Records. The band appeared in the movie Clueless. In 1997, the success of their single "The Impression That I Get" and its follow up, "The Rascal King" earned them mainstream recognition. In 2000 they put out their critically acclaimed disk Pay Attention. The Mighty Mighty Bosstones released their last album on Side One Dummy Records. They officially went on hiatus in 2003, citing too much time on the road and desire to branch out and do different things. In 2007, the Bosstones announced that they were reforming. They played their 10th Hometown Throwdown in Boston and released a new album, Medium Rare, which consists of rare B-sides, and 3 new songs, including the single, "Don't Worry Desmond Dekker". The band announced their split in early 2022. Read more on Last.fm. User-contributed text is available under the Creative Commons By-SA License; additional terms may apply.

perplexity.description:
Devil's Night Out" is the debut studio album by The Mighty Mighty Bosstones, released on August 22, 1989, by Taang! Records. The album is a foundational work in the ska-punk genre, blending fast-paced punk rock energy with prominent ska rhythms and horn-driven melodies. Characterized by its aggressive tempos, catchy hooks, and the band's signature horn section, the album helped define the sound that would become synonymous with the Bosstones and the broader Boston ska scene.

As the band's first full-length release, "Devil's Night Out" established The Mighty Mighty Bosstones as key players in the late 1980s American ska revival. It set the stage for their subsequent success and influence within the genre, showcasing their ability to merge punk's raw intensity with ska's danceable grooves. While the album did not achieve major commercial success upon its original release, it was well-received by critics and fans for its originality and energy, earning a reputation as a cult classic and an essential early document of American ska-punk.
